engineering.title:
The interface is the beginning.
The engineering goes deeper.
engineering.description: MediConnect’s source brings together role-based applications, backend services and infrastructure as code. The public site is a lightweight showcase; the larger architecture is retained for technical review.

items.title: Role-aware applications
items.body: Patient, clinician, staff and administrator interfaces, with protected routes in the application source.

items.title: Connected service design
items.body: Appointment, record, communication and AI integrations are preserved. They are not activated by this demo.

items.title: Infrastructure as evidence
items.body: Kubernetes, Terraform and CI/CD definitions remain available in the project, alongside retired Aurora/RDS and Secrets Manager integrations.

engineering.note: Architecture and security controls are implementation work, not a claim of regulatory certification.

items.question: Can I book a real appointment?
items.answer: No. This deployment is an interactive portfolio, not an operating healthcare service. Booking, authentication, payments, video calls and AI services are not available here.

items.question: Is the patient information real?
items.answer: No. Names, dates and records in these previews are fictional examples. Please do not enter personal, medical or payment information into this showcase.

items.question: What happened to the cloud infrastructure?
items.answer: Costly cloud resources were intentionally retired. Their code is preserved as engineering evidence, including Kubernetes, CI/CD, Aurora/RDS and Secrets Manager integrations.

items.question: Does the preview send anything to a backend?
items.answer: The care-stage and role previews use local interface state only. They do not create appointments, store patient records, call AI services or charge payments.
